2025.clinched: Barcelona three-hour finale, October 2025, final round
2025.note: Van der Linde and Weerts won the Barcelona finale outright to take the 2025 overall title, sharing the #32 BMW with Ugo de Wilde, and the same result gave Team WRT the overall teams' championship. The car had three wins and four more podiums across the season. Behind them, WRT filled the podium's second step with the AlManar entry of Jens Klingmann, Al Faisal Al Zubair and Ben Tuck, which took the Gold Cup team title, while Augusto Farfus, Jesse Krohn and Raffaele Marciello were third for ROWE.

2024.clinched: 6 Hours of Jeddah, November 2024, final round
2024.note: Auer and Engel went to the Jeddah finale behind Dries Vanthoor and Charles Weerts in the combined standings and won the race to overturn it, sharing the #48 Mercedes-AMG with Daniel Morad. They took the lead in the third hour when Auer leapfrogged Valentino Rossi during a round of pit stops, and finished 7.971 seconds clear of the Grasser Lamborghini. Vanthoor and Weerts could only manage fourth, which cost them the overall crown but not the teams' title. The separate Endurance Cup went to Alessandro Pier Guidi and Alessio Rovera without their winning a race all year.

2023.note: Marciello and Boguslavskiy settled the 2023 overall championship at Zandvoort with a round still to run, finishing the ten-round season on 194.5 points to the 156.5 of Mattia Drudi and Ricardo Feller. At the Barcelona finale that followed they added the Endurance Cup, fifth place being enough for a title they shared with Jules Gounon after wins at Le Castellet and the Nürburgring. It was a third overall crown for Marciello, after 2018 and 2022, and a second for Boguslavskiy, after 2020.

2022.note: Marciello took the 2022 overall title at the Sprint Cup finale in Valencia, with the Endurance round at Barcelona still to come. He dominated the second qualifying session for his fourth pole in five sprint races, then drove the opening stint in heavy rain and built a lead of around seventeen seconds; his team-mate Timur Boguslavskiy lost two places in the wet, and third place at the flag was enough. He won the Spa 24 Hours the same year, and went on to take the Endurance Cup at Barcelona as well.

2021.note: Vanthoor and Weerts became overall champions in the Endurance Cup race at the Nürburgring, sharing an Audi R8 with Robin Frijns: they started twelfth and were sixth after three hours, which was enough with two races left. A week earlier they had taken their second consecutive Sprint Cup title at Brands Hatch with a round in hand, 42.5 points clear, which made them the most successful pairing in Sprint Cup history. Team WRT completed the set by winning the overall teams' championship at Valencia three weeks later.

2020.clinched: Circuit Paul Ricard 1000km, November 2020, final round
2020.note: Boguslavskiy arrived at the Paul Ricard finale on 137 points, 24 clear of Charles Weerts and Dries Vanthoor, needing fifth place to be certain. He did not get it: the AKKA ASP Mercedes was in the mix early, lost a minute in the pits to a damaged splitter and dropped out of the points, which also cost the team the combined teams' championship to Team WRT. It made no difference to the drivers' title, and at 20 he became the youngest overall champion the series has had. Ferrari took its first Endurance Cup the same afternoon.

2019.note: Caldarelli and Mapelli had to win the Barcelona three-hour finale on 29 September 2019 to have any chance, and they did, with Albert Costa standing in for the ill Dennis Lind. The SMP Ferrari crew that led the Endurance Cup needed only eighth: Mikhail Aleshin picked up a puncture in contact with a Mercedes and fell to fortieth, and Miguel Molina then took a drive-through for hitting a Bentley at the final chicane. Maro Engel and Luca Stolz failed to score in the overall fight, leaving the Lamborghini pair 23 points clear, and they became the first drivers to win the overall, Endurance and GT World Challenge Europe titles in one season.

2018.note: Marciello, already the Sprint Cup champion, led the overall standings of what was then the Blancpain GT Series by 18.5 points and needed eight of them at Barcelona. He ran from sixth to third in the opening hour and the #88 AKKA ASP Mercedes finished second, which settled the overall title in 2018 and denied him the Endurance Cup: the race, and that championship, went to the Black Falcon Mercedes of Maro Engel, Luca Stolz and Yelmer Buurman, whom his team-mate Tristan Vautier pressured to the flag. Winning it would have completed a sweep of all three titles, which nobody had done.

2017.note: Bortolotti and Engelhart went to the Barcelona finale of the 2017 Blancpain GT Series leading the overall standings comfortably but eight points down in the Endurance Cup, and a gearbox failure decided both. The Bentley of Andy Soucek, Maxime Soulet and Vincent Abril had qualified poorly, recovered into the top ten, then broke halfway through and was parked, which made the overall title certain; third place at the flag gave the Lamborghini pair the Endurance Cup as well, shared with Andrea Caldarelli. The race went to the AKKA ASP Mercedes of Félix Serrallés, Tristan Vautier and Daniel Juncadella.

2016.note: Baumann and Buhk took the 2016 overall title with eighth place and four points in the first Barcelona finale the series had held. They had retaken the standings lead with fourth in the Nürburgring endurance race after losing it to bad luck at Paul Ricard, and arrived five points ahead of Rob Bell, whose McLaren started sixteenth after a qualifying-race drive-through and recovered only to thirteenth. Unable to pass a Phoenix Audi in the lower half of the top ten, the HTP pair scored just enough: 134 points, ten clear of Bell and 22 clear of Laurens Vanthoor, and the teams' title as well.

2015.note: Frijns was crowned overall champion of the 2015 Blancpain GT Series at Zandvoort, at home, in the last event of the year, and he came within a few hundredths of a second of a double. The Sprint Series title came down to him against Vincent Abril and Maximilian Buhk once a warm-up engine failure ended Norbert Siedler's challenge, and Buhk took the chequered flag just ahead of Frijns's Audi, which handed that championship to the HTP pair. Belgian Audi Club Team WRT took the Sprint Series teams' title. It was Frijns's fourth title in four seasons.

2014.clinched: Baku World Challenge, November 2014, final round of the Sprint Series
2014.note: The overall title existed for the first time in 2014, awarded to whoever scored most across the new sprint series and the endurance series together, and Vanthoor won it at the Baku finale. He and César Ramos led the main race from lights to flag in the #1 WRT Audi, holding off the Beechdean Aston Martin of Jonny Adam and Andy Soucek, while Maximilian Buhk, who needed fifth to take the title, was put out by an incident. Vanthoor had already won the Endurance Series Pro Cup at the Nürburgring 1000 and the Spa 24 Hours that year.
